correctness.rationale: For each excluded singleton valuation V\{v}, the image s(v) contains a private coordinate, giving m distinct forced atoms. The remaining shared coordinate support sets are graph cliques covering all edges, giving n>=m+theta_e. Conversely assign m private vertex atoms and one atom per clique in an optimal edge-cover, then represent every truth set by all shared atoms plus exactly its true-vertex private atoms. This gives graph-isomorphism and all Boolean-valued assignments. Source Lemma 5.2 supplies the parameterized-sentence interpretation. All cases m>=1 including edgeless and complete graphs are handled; verify.py brute-forces all valuations through m=3 and constructs all m=4 labelled graphs, with large-m truth resting on proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest 2026 co-consistency frame-embedding theorem gives m+|E| coordinates but does not optimize them. The edge clique-cover interpretation of ordinary intersection numbers is established classic graph theory and is not claimed new. This result combines the unrestricted Boolean-containment valuation requirement with exact forced private markers and an optimal shared clique-cover budget, giving a sharp total atom count for each finite reflexive symmetric frame.

value.rationale: The atom budget is a natural exact resource invariant of uniform finite modal frame simulation, not an arbitrary finite list. It replaces the source's m+|E| edge-token bound by sharp m+theta_e without sacrificing any valuation, an asymptotically quadratic-to-linear savings for complete frames and a proof of no possible savings on triangle-free frames. It cleanly reduces optimization of finite Boolean co-consistency presentations to edge clique cover, a mathematically motivated and nontrivial graph invariant.
